subject: Re: Encord Trial + Slack
text:
Hi William and Jennifer,
Quick follow-up from our last demo. You showed a CLIP-based similarity
search, and I wanted to confirm whether that’s the main (or only) way
embedding-based similarity is intended to be used for data curation, or if
there are other user-driven workflows as well.

A few quick clarifying questions to help us scope this correctly:

   -

   What data unit are embeddings computed on (e.g., annotated object
   instances such as bounding boxes, versus frames or clips)?
   -

   Can users pick a specific sample as a query (seed) to find visually
   similar samples?
   -

   Where does this live in the UI, and how much control do users have?

For context, one use case we care about is starting from known failure
cases and finding other visually similar or confusing negatives, rather
than general dataset browsing.

Thanks!

Yang

text:
Hi Shivant,

So far so good, I hope your 2026 has started nicely as well!

I think the agent can help, thank you for the idea. We have a specific
methodology where each exam can have different types of images, and each
image is a kind of topographic map. For each image, we have metadata that
is necessary for the SME to do the annotation, and we want to show that
information during the annotation process, ideally in the same UI where
they are doing the annotation. We can have up to 5 types of metadata that
we want to give, not necessarily all 5 in each image, and up to 3 or 4
types of images per exam.

 Thank you,

subject: Re: Fluint Business Case updates
text:
Ray, something to think on re: pilot.

If we're trying to boost early stage conversions, we need to test how Olli improves reps' discovery preparation and gap analysis. For late stage: Watson already said the business case was pretty good and the gaps were relevant. Having Olli work alongside the deal start-finish should result in stronger business cases given the ability to fill in the gaps as we go.

Feels like the next step is a broader test group with more variance in performance. Olli comes with a high degree of sales acumen and continues to learn from closed-won deals, serving those learnings back to all reps and closing the delta on performance.

What do you think about starting with the UK team (Leo + 5 commercial reps)? That gives you a diverse test group and the ability to see impact on intro-to-deal conversion before your new hire class starts. If we're seeing real lift by mid-March, you'd have proof to roll out to CK's US team and the new hires.

When does that new hire cohort plan to start?
+
Thoughts on this as a plan?

John Earls
Account Executive @Fluint
